synopsis: EMESRT’s PR-5A turns vehicle interactions into standard scenarios and provides a nine-level control model originating from a group of mining companies [f11571, f11572, f11736]. A 2019 trade article reports 24 surface vehicle-interaction scenarios; the corpus distinguishes these from 17 published surface storyboards, so the counts measure different things [f6232, f6234]. Chapter 8 identifies PR-5A as Rev 3.0, dated September 2024, citing a Wabtec white paper; EMESRT’s 2024 activity report confirms the September update but does not independently state the revision number [f5925, f6231, f6235]. For a team starting from zero in October 2026, an operating-domain definition and scenario catalogue mapped to PR-5A and ISO 21815-3 risk areas is considered realistic by mid-2027, including a machine-by-scenario-by-environment-by-sensor-condition taxonomy [f831].

relations.note: Both identify Rev 3.0 and September 2024; f6231 names the cited source.
Both attribute the nine-level vehicle-interaction control model to EMESRT’s PR-5A.
The 2019 report supplies a count and surface scope for the standard scenarios.
Explains why 24 scenarios should not be equated with 17 published storyboards.
Confirms the September 2024 update, but not the claimed revision number.
PR-5A’s standard scenarios provide a basis for the planned mapped scenario catalogue.
